watchOS 27 will launch this fall as the next major update for Apple Watch, introducing a practical new feature to extend Apple Watch battery life: "Active Battery Extension Notification."

watchOS 27 can proactively extend Apple Watch battery life by disabling unused features

watchOS 27 is on the way, bringing two new apps, a useful new tap gesture, a default new home screen layout, three health-related upgrades, and more to Apple Watch.

Another new addition in watchOS 27 aims to extend your Apple Watch battery life.

"Active Battery Extension Notification" is a brand-new type of alert that may appear on your Apple Watch.

When you receive a battery extension notification, it means watchOS 27 has detected certain features you've never used, and disabling them will help conserve battery life.

These features include Gestures, the "Raise to Speak" function for invoking Siri, and "Start Workout" reminders.

Each of these features involves background processing, which places a certain drain on battery life.

Therefore, in watchOS 27, if the system detects that you have never used these features, it will automatically disable them and send a "Battery Extension Notification" to inform you of the change, giving you the option to keep them enabled.

If you do use these features regularly, you won't receive this notification. Of course, you can also go to Settings at any time to disable them yourself in exchange for longer battery life.

Apple did not specify how much extra battery life disabling these features will actually provide, but it's clear the power savings are worth them building this brand-new battery extension feature.

Apple's first foldable iPhone is set to debut this autumn, with reports indicating the new device will be named the iPhone Ultra. Below is a roundup of six major selling points expected from this new premium iPhone Ultra.

Design: Book-style folding, titanium body, crease-free display

As Apple's first foldable device, the iPhone Ultra will stand out distinctly within the iPhone lineup.

Unlike most foldable phones on the market, the iPhone Ultra will be wider when unfolded than when folded. It adopts a book-style folding design, with the cover screen featuring a shorter and wider aspect ratio than current iPhone displays, while the inner screen's size and shape are similar to those of an iPad mini.

Additionally, the iPhone Ultra's inner screen is expected to feature a crease-free design, which would be a major breakthrough for the entire foldable device market.

The iPhone Ultra's design will draw on elements from the iPhone Air, such as a titanium frame. When unfolded, the body will be extremely slim, and when folded, it will resemble two iPhone Airs stacked together, but even lighter and thinner.

Display: Unique size and orientation

The iPhone Ultra will come with two displays: one on the outer body and another that appears only when unfolded. Rumoured sizes are as follows:

  • Outer display: 5.3 to 5.5 inches
  • Inner display: 7.6 to 7.8 inches

The outer display is similar in size to the iPhone mini, but with a wider aspect ratio.

The inner display, meanwhile, offers a holding experience very close to that of an iPad mini.

Cameras: Two main cameras plus two front-facing cameras

The iPhone Ultra will feature two rear cameras, including a 48-megapixel main camera and a 48-megapixel ultra-wide camera.

In other words, users who opt for the Ultra instead of the Pro model will lose access to the telephoto lens and its stronger zoom capabilities.

Since the iPhone Ultra has two displays, it will also come with two front-facing cameras, one for each screen.

The specs of these front cameras have yet to be confirmed, but Apple is likely to adopt the 18-megapixel Center Stage front camera first introduced on the iPhone 17 last year, with a punch-hole design expected.

Software: iOS 27 multitasking features

iOS 27 is expected to add a number of iPhone Ultra-exclusive features, with details likely to be revealed this autumn.

According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, two major upgrades are coming:

  • Support for side-by-side multitasking with apps
  • An iPad-like app layout

There are already hints in iOS 27, as Apple has added landscape orientation support to several iPhone apps.

Apple silicon: A20 Pro processor with C2 modem chip

The iPhone Ultra is expected to feature the new A20 Pro processor and C2 modem chip, both of which are also likely to appear in the iPhone 18 Pro.

The A20 Pro uses an all-new 2-nanometre process and combines WMCM (wafer-level multi-chip module) packaging technology to further boost performance, with upgrades expected to be more significant than ever.

The new processor will come with 12GB of RAM, the same as the A19 Pro, but will use faster LPDDR5 memory, delivering overall better performance.

The C2 is Apple's brand-new in-house cellular modem chip, expected to replace Qualcomm's 5G modem and bring several new advantages.

Touch ID

It would seem odd for a model named "Ultra" not to support Face ID, but according to reports, Apple's foldable iPhone will not include Face ID. Instead, Apple will bring back Touch ID, integrating the fingerprint sensor into the power button.

The Touch ID implementation on the iPhone Ultra will be very similar to that used on the iPad Air and iPad mini.

Reports suggest that due to the body's ultra-slim design, Apple has been unable to shrink two separate Face ID modules (one for each display) small enough to fit inside the device. Whether future models can achieve this remains to be seen.

iPhone Ultra pricing and conclusion

Market rumours about the iPhone Ultra's pricing vary widely. Most analysts expect the 256GB version to start at around US$1,999 (approximately HK$15,600).

Whatever the final price turns out to be, one thing is almost certain: this will be the most expensive iPhone ever. Apple is essentially combining an iPhone and an iPad into one device, and clearly expects the price to be justified.

Apple Pay is the go-to feature for iPhone users when shopping in stores, online, and in apps. Apple recently announced four new features that make Apple Pay even more useful. Here's how they work.

iOS 27 新設計

One of my favorite changes in iOS 27 is the redesigned Apple Pay checkout interface. The new interface makes it easier to switch between different credit cards during the checkout flow on websites and in apps.

With the new design, you can swipe to switch between credit cards directly on the main Apple Pay checkout screen. You can also tap on a card to view all available Apple Pay credit cards in a grid layout.

The new design also makes it easier to view individual credit card information, including rewards, balances, buy now, pay later options, and more.

iOS 27 is now available as a developer and public beta, with an expected official launch this fall.

美國運通獎賞積分

Apple and American Express recently announced a new partnership that allows you to pay using American Express Membership Rewards points.

When using an American Express card to shop online or in apps, you'll see a new "Use Rewards" option that displays your current Membership Rewards points balance. You can use points to pay for all or part of your purchase directly within the Apple Pay checkout flow.

Amex points redeemed through Apple Pay are valued at 0.7 cents per point. For example, 10,000 points can be converted into $70 to offset your purchase amount.

一拍即傳

In iOS 27, Apple is adding a brand-new "Tap to Provision" feature that works with Apple Pay on iPhone for in-store shopping.

This feature is an extension of the iPhone Tap to Pay functionality, which Apple expects to launch this fall. Apple explains:

Customers can simply tap to connect with a participating merchant's iPhone, enjoying a more personalized and faster in-store shopping experience, and securely share email and other contact information, shipping addresses, membership rewards information, and more. Customers can also view items in their shopping basket in real time, keep track of what they've purchased, and ensure all discounts and offers are applied correctly.

Once complete, customers can use Apple Pay on their own iPhone to complete checkout.

為扣賬卡增值

Later this year, iPhone users will be able to manage debit card balances directly within the Apple Pay interface.

According to Apple, you'll be able to top up supported debit cards directly through Apple Pay in Apple Wallet or at checkout.

總結

As Apple Pay becomes more widespread and adopted by more retailers, it's great to see Apple continuing to improve the user experience. Personally, whether shopping online or in stores, Apple Pay is essentially my go-to payment method.

Magnet Forensics 正就 Paradigm Shift Technology 發佈 usbliter8 一事提出訴訟，指控該無法修補的漏洞涉及多款 Apple SoC，而其開發過程涉及一名前工程師盜用商業機密。以下為詳情。

Magnet 聲稱前工程師洩露了內部漏洞研究資料

上個月，Paradigm Shift 的研究人員公開了 usbliter8 的技術細節。這是一個全新的、無法修補的 iPhone BootROM 漏洞，能夠在搭載 Apple A12 及 A13 晶片的裝置上執行任意代碼。

該漏洞影響 A12、S4、S5 及 A13 SoC。它利用特製數據混淆裝置的 USB 控制器，讓取得實體接觸權限的攻擊者掌控裝置的啟動過程。

攻擊者其後可在 iOS 載入之前執行自製代碼，繞過簽署檢查，並啟動經修改的系統軟件。

由於 usbliter8 針對 BootROM 發動攻擊，因此無法透過軟件更新修復。不過，其實際影響相對有限，因為只影響 Apple 於 2018 年及 2019 年推出的舊款晶片。

Paradigm Shift 當時表示，是次漏洞披露已與 Apple 產品安全團隊協調。然而，Magnet Forensics 現時聲稱 usbliter8 源自其前工程師從事的機密工作，該工程師其後加入了 Paradigm Shift。

訴訟內容摘錄如下：

被告 Mario Del Gaudio 於 2023 年 11 月至 2024 年 11 月期間擔任派駐至 Magnet Forensics 的漏洞工程師。在任職期間，Del Gaudio 被指派參與 Magnet Forensics 其中一項最敏感的內部專有能力——一項內部代號為「MSG」的零日入侵能力。在派駐 Magnet Forensics 的工作結束後，Del Gaudio 隨即加入被告 Paradigm Shift——一家從事入侵能力商業化的科技及網絡安全公司。於 2026 年 6 月 18 日，Paradigm Shift 發佈題為「Introducing usbliter8: An A12/A13 SecureROM Exploit」的詳細技術網誌文章，公開了大量技術細節，內容本質上與 Del Gaudio 早前在 Magnet Forensics 從事、代號 MSG 的專有能力相同。

Magnet Forensics 聲稱已掌握 Del Gaudio 與 usbliter8 漏洞發佈直接相關的證據，並指 Paradigm Shift 多次無視其要求撤回文章及概念驗證代碼的停止侵權通知。

除了要求刪除 usbliter8 相關文章及材料外，Magnet Forensics 亦尋求經濟賠償，以及法院頒令禁止進一步使用或披露其所指的商業機密。

《華爾街日報》報道，美光正施壓特朗普政府，阻止蘋果向中國供應商採購記憶體晶片的計劃。以下是詳情。

蘋果的中國晶片計劃將不限於中國市場

上個月，正值蘋果因持續的記憶體短缺而上調多款產品價格前夕，蒂姆·庫克接受《華爾街日報》訪問時表示，美國應重新考慮限制部分中國供應商的做法。

其後數天，《華爾街日報》報道指蘋果早已向政府申請許可，擬向中國長鑫存儲（CXMT）採購晶片。與此同時，《金融時報》報道蘋果正與長江存儲（YMTC）洽商採購晶片事宜。《金融時報》其後更指蘋果已在測試長鑫存儲的DRAM晶片。

背景資料顯示，長鑫存儲及長江存儲均被美國國防部列為中國軍方企業，而長江存儲亦被商務部列入實體清單。

這並非完全禁止蘋果在其非美國銷售的產品中使用相關晶片，但令任何潛在交易在政治上變得敏感，過往亦因此引發外界對蘋果的批評。

《華爾街日報》最新報道指，隨着蘋果持續向特朗普政府施壓，希望獲准在非中國市場（即美國境外銷售的產品）使用中國記憶體晶片，美光正進行游說，反對有關計劃，要求官員加以阻撓。

報道內容如下：

知情人士透露，過去數星期，蘋果行政總裁蒂姆·庫克及多名高層向特朗普，以及商務部長霍華德·盧特尼克及財政部長斯科特·貝森特等官員，推銷一項計劃，建議在美國境外銷售的蘋果產品中使用中國長鑫存儲及長江存儲的記憶體晶片。美光作為美國唯一具規模的記憶體晶片製造商，對此提出反駁。美光行政總裁桑賈伊·梅赫羅特拉等高層警告盧特尼克及其他政府官員，指若容許長鑫存儲及其他中國企業向美國科技公司供貨，不論銷售地區為何，均可能重演中國在摧毀美國鋼鐵及製造業方面所扮演的角色，令本土產業遭受滅頂之災。

簡而言之，反對蘋果計劃的理據是：即使僅在中國市場向獲國家大力補貼的中國供應商採購記憶體，最終亦可能削弱美國生產商的競爭力，打擊本土產業。

此外，《華爾街日報》亦報道，美光表示可透過加快本土廠房建設及增加美國投資，協助紓緩晶片短缺問題。

數星期前，美光一名高層曾向《華爾街日報》表示，蘋果進取的採購策略助長了今次記憶體短缺的問題，指2023年市場低迷期間，「部分」客戶在定價上「非常進取」。他續稱，這些極低價格令業界不願投資擴充產能，為今天的供應緊張埋下伏筆。

回到報道，《華爾街日報》指蘋果與美光之間的爭議令特朗普政府處於尷尬境地，因為「這場游說戰將迫使特朗普在兩大經濟優先目標之間作出取捨：降低美國消費者價格，以及提升本土半導體產能以減少對其他國家的依賴。」

蘋果方面，過去兩年大部分時間均大力宣傳其投資項目，包括6,000億美元的「美國製造計劃」（American Manufacturing Program），以及與英特達的合作，近期亦公佈了與博通的300億美元協議。

外界普遍認為，這些開支旨在為蘋果與政府建立良好關係，積累政治資本，以平衡其向受限制中國供應商採購記憶體晶片等具爭議性的要求。

另一方面，美光的估值則跟隨整體記憶體市場走勢。年初至今，其股價上升191%，過去12個月更飆升727%，惟近週波動加劇。目前股價較6月底的歷史高位低23%，單日亦下跌6.99%。

白宮發言人回應《華爾街日報》查詢時，未有就政府如何平衡蘋果與美光之間的優先事項作明確表態，僅表示將致力「為美國民眾帶來投資及經濟紓困，同時捍衛國家安全」。

Apple @ Work 專欄由 Mosyle 獨家呈獻——這是業界唯一的 Apple 統一平台。Mosyle 是唯一將所有必要功能整合於單一專業級平台的解決方案，能在企業環境中無縫且自動化地部署、管理及保護 Apple 裝置。全球超過 45,000 間機構信賴 Mosyle，以輕鬆且經濟實惠的方式，讓數百萬部 Apple 裝置即時投入使用。立即申請延長試用，了解 Mosyle 為何是你處理 Apple 裝置所需的一切。

在企業或零售環境部署數碼看板時，IT 團隊往往面臨兩難：花錢購買像 Apple TV 這類高階機頂盒，還是以廉價 Android 裝置節省前期開支。Kitcast 發表的最新《2026 年數碼看板現況報告》提供了針對此情況的大量遙測數據，結果清晰顯示，在企業可靠性（尤其在規模化部署時）方面，Apple TV 是更出色的選擇。

關於 Apple @ Work：Bradley Chambers 自 2009 年起一直擔任 Apple IT 系統管理員。憑藉在部署及管理防火牆、交換器、流動裝置管理系統、企業級 WiFi、以至數千部 Mac 和 iPad 的豐富經驗，他將分享 Apple IT 管理員如何部署 Apple 裝置、建構支援網絡、培訓用戶，以及從 IT 管理的實戰經驗中分享故事，並探討 Apple 可以如何為 IT 部門進一步改善產品。

廉價硬件的真正代價

Kitcast 在這份報告中分析了來自 1,000 部 Apple TV 及 250 部 Android 裝置、為期 12 個月的遙測數據。數據顯示，當把維護及更換成本計算在內，低價 Android 棒所帶來的價格優勢便會徹底消失。我自己在這兩方面都略有經驗，稍後會跟大家分享。

根據報告，Apple TV 裝置的 12 個月平均正常運行時間中位數達到 99%；相比之下，Android 裝置只有 96%。雖然這個差距看似不大，但對實際使用時間的影響卻非常顯著。在 Apple TV 裝置中，10 部有 7 部能維持 99% 或以上的正常運行時間，基本上無需重新開機等操作就能保持運作。Android 播放器方面，只有 12% 能達到同樣水平，而近三分之一的裝置正常運行時間更跌至 95% 以下。

對於管理大規模環境的 IT 團隊來說，可靠性問題會迅速累積惡化。數據顯示，Android 裝置平均每年會離線 15.2 次，需要 IT 人員介入處理；而 Apple TV 平均每年只有 5.3 次離線事件。

硬件故障在 Android 裝置上亦遠比 Apple TV 普遍。Kitcast 發現 Android 裝置的年度更換率為 18%，而 Apple TV 裝置的更換率僅為 2%。

9to5Mac 觀點

目前，我管理著一個以 Android 為基礎的數碼看板顯示屏。我從一個承傳下來、由供應商部署的 Firestick 方案，轉為向供應商租用專用機頂盒。雖然它是 Android 系統，但除非你親眼看到開機過程，否則根本不會察覺。我喜歡它作為單一用途裝置的定位，但我也遇過不少問題。大部分裝置都需要不時重新啟動，事實上供應商可以設定每日定時重新啟動。這也並非 HDMI 連接的問題，而是某種記憶體洩漏之類的毛病。有了零接觸部署及完善的管理功能，Apple TV 持續證明自己是真正的企業級裝置。最近 Apple TV 加價的幅度相當驚人，我很希望 Apple 能推出一款低價的「棒狀」裝置，以滿足企業數碼看板的需求。我透過裝置管理所管理的 Apple TV 確實非常好用。雖然最近的加價令人肉痛，但數據顯示，不論價格如何上調，Apple TV 仍然是出色的數碼看板工具。

Earlier this year, Apple decided to discontinue the Pro Display XDR entirely. Despite its impressive hardware, the monitor had not been updated for years and still retails for over US$6,000. Apple's new display lineup now consists of the Studio Display and the brand-new Studio Display XDR. While each has its own highlights, both are currently only available with a 27-inch 5K screen. The XDR starts at a hefty US$3,299, and with upgrades, it can reach US$3,600 before tax. This has left a gap in the market for other manufacturers to offer larger-sized Retina-class displays for Mac users — and that's exactly where the brand-new Meirro Pro comes in. The Meirro Pro is a 32-inch 6K display built with a full aluminum chassis, supports single-cable connection, and comes with an adjustable stand — all for just US$1,199. I've been using it as my primary monitor, and although Meirro has made a few compromises to keep the price down, it may well be the most compelling Studio Display alternative I've tested. Here's everything you need to know.

Be sure to check out our hands-on video of the Meirro Pro for a closer look at this product!

Design and Specifications

The first thing that stands out is how remarkably similar it looks to the current Apple Studio Display. This monitor fits naturally into any Apple-styled desk setup. It's crafted from fully CNC-machined aluminum and comes with an adjustable stand made of the same material, giving it an exceptionally premium feel. The build quality inspires confidence throughout your entire setup. Most non-Apple displays on the market use plastic enclosures with stands that often feel flimsy — but the Meirro Pro uses absolutely no plastic anywhere on the device.

Unboxing and setup are also refreshingly straightforward. Simply attach the base to the stand, secure the stand to the back of the display, plug in the power, and it's ready to go. The design is extremely minimalist, with no buttons at all, and most importantly, the power supply is built into the monitor. This means there's no bulky external power brick dangling from the cable, keeping your desk setup wonderfully clean. Both the adjustable stand and VESA mount are included in the box at no extra cost. So yes, this is a product heavily inspired by Apple's design language — and it absolutely delivers on my expectations.

But how does it actually perform in terms of display quality? As I mentioned at the start, this is a true 6K panel. It uses a 32-inch Nano IPS Black panel with a resolution of 6144 × 3456, which works out to 224 ppi — delivering true Retina-level sharpness. Here are the key specifications:

  • 32-inch Nano IPS Black panel
  • 6144 × 3456 resolution
  • 224 PPI
  • 60Hz refresh rate
  • 2,000:1 contrast ratio
  • 10-bit color supporting over 1.07 billion colors
  • 98% DCI-P3 color gamut
  • 99.5% Adobe RGB color gamut
  • Typical brightness of 450 nits, HDR peak brightness of 750 nits

The panel is only available with a glossy anti-reflective coating as the sole option. While I would have liked a matte coating as an alternative, even in a brightly lit room with plenty of windows, the glossy coating still performs admirably.

Ports and Accessories

Similar to Apple's display offerings, the Meirro Pro keeps its port selection minimal — the back features only five USB-C ports for all I/O. One of these serves as the primary upstream connection, supporting DisplayPort 2.1 with bandwidth up to 80Gbps, and can deliver up to 96W of power passthrough to keep your MacBook charged at all times. This means a single cable handles the entire 6K video signal. The remaining four USB-C ports are downstream ports with limited data transfer speeds — all at USB 2.0 specification. However, they're more than adequate for connecting webcams, speakers, and other peripherals.

Since the Meirro Pro has no buttons whatsoever (not even a power button), a remote control closely resembling the previous-generation Apple TV remote is included in the box. This remote features a power button and provides access to the display's system settings when needed.

My Experience and Setup

I've had the Meirro Pro set up as the sole primary display on my desk, and the experience has been outstanding. The 32-inch screen size combined with 6K resolution satisfies all my expectations for a high-end Mac monitor — both in terms of physical real estate and pixel density.

My setup is quite simple. I personally use multiple external SSDs and prefer the Satechi Thunderbolt hub, so I connect the display through that hub. One Thunderbolt cable runs from the display to the hub, and another Thunderbolt cable runs from the hub to my MacBook Pro. Everything works exactly as expected.

I've tested this display across all my daily workflows, and it handles them with ease. Working in Final Cut Pro — including editing timelines and organizing media files — the extra screen space has been a tremendous help. A large part of my daily work involves research, requiring numerous tabs and windows open simultaneously; the higher pixel density makes the screen feel even larger than its actual 32-inch size. The most important feature of this display is its 224 PPI, which allows macOS — and even iPadOS — to scale exactly as Apple intended.

One last thing worth mentioning is that the solid build quality helps reduce monitor wobble. Most displays on the market shake when you type at your desk, and this becomes especially noticeable with a sit-stand desk like mine. The combination of premium materials and a sturdy stand effectively minimizes this wobble. So, whether judged by specs or real-world use, the Meirro Pro has every reason to serve as a Studio Display alternative. However, at this price point, there are some compromises worth addressing.

The Compromises

I'll say it again — a 32-inch 6K display with CNC aluminum construction for under US$1,200 sounds almost too good to be true. Meirro had to make some tough decisions to bring the price down to this level. Since most potential buyers will compare it to the Studio Display, it's important to point out the features it lacks. The Meirro Pro does not include or support:

  • Built-in webcam
  • Speakers
  • Microphone
  • No daisy-chaining support

Personally, these compromises are well worth the savings, since I already own external webcams and speakers. The lack of a microphone doesn't affect me much either, as I use AirPods or a Shure microphone when needed. Still, I want to highlight these details so prospective buyers have a clearer picture.

The final compromise I noticed concerns the speed of the USB-C ports on the back of the display. The Apple Studio Display offers a total of four USB-C ports — two of which are Thunderbolt, and the other two at USB 3.0 speeds. The Meirro Pro offers more USB-C ports overall, but only one is Thunderbolt, while the remaining four are the slower USB 2.0 specification. For me, this isn't a major issue because I have the Satechi Thunderbolt dock; however, I understand that some users may need faster ports.

Even taking these compromises into account, I still believe the Meirro Pro is an unequivocal recommendation over the Apple Studio Display, because the value it offers is simply too high.

Price and Availability

The Meirro Pro is priced at US$1,299 as standard, and is currently available for pre-order at US$1,199. Shipping is expected to begin on August 1st. If you already have a monitor arm, you can opt out of the included stand to save US$50, bringing the total down to US$1,149. The US$1,199 price includes:

  • Meirro Pro display
  • Aluminum stand
  • VESA mount
  • USB-C cable
  • Power cable
  • Remote control

Conclusion

The Meirro Pro is the best true Studio Display alternative I've ever tested. For just US$1,199, you get a 32-inch 6K display with Retina-level sharpness, a glossy Nano IPS Black panel, a full aluminum body, single-cable Mac connectivity, an adjustable stand, and a VESA mount. If you're after Apple's most complete all-in-one desktop experience, the Studio Display still has its merits; but if you already own some external accessories and truly value screen size, resolution, build quality, and value for money, the Meirro Pro is an absolutely worthwhile recommendation.

What do you think? Would you consider this display? Do you already own a Studio Display? Do you miss the Pro Display XDR? I'd love to hear your thoughts. And remember — be sure to watch our video to experience its real-world performance firsthand!

Apple的年度iPhone發布會大約在每年九月舉行，距離現在還有兩個月左右。不過今年情況將有所不同——並非整個iPhone系列同時推出，而是只有iPhone 18 Pro、iPhone 18 Pro Max，以及全新的摺疊iPhone會在今年九月亮相。原因是這樣的。

iPhone系列越來越龐大

過去幾年，每年的iPhone陣容不斷擴大。幾年前，每年只有3款新機：iPhone 11、iPhone 11 Pro和iPhone 11 Pro Max。2020年增至4款，加入了iPhone 12 mini；2022年iPhone 12 mini被iPhone 14 Plus取代，而iPhone 14 Plus之後又被iPhone Air取代。

隨著iPhone 16e的推出，每年的發布數量增至5部。如果再加入iPhone Ultra，每年就會有6部iPhone。機型數量之多，如果一次過推出，舞台肯定會非常擁擠。

因此，Apple決定改為分階段發布。

兩次iPhone發布：秋季與春季

iPhone 18系列將會有6款型號：iPhone 18、iPhone 18 Pro、iPhone 18 Pro Max、iPhone 18e、iPhone Air 2，以及iPhone Ultra。

這個分階段發布有一個主題：旗艦機秋季推出，低階機春季推出。具體安排如下：

  • 2026年秋季：iPhone 18 Pro、iPhone 18 Pro Max、iPhone Ultra
  • 2027年春季：iPhone 18、iPhone 18e、iPhone Air 2

當iPhone系列擴展到4款的時候，第四部機在開售時從來都賣得不好，無論是iPhone mini還是iPhone Plus都是如此。所以Apple認為應該明確分開——為多出來的機款設立獨立的焦點。

不過談到iPhone 18就有點轉折。據報Apple正研究將iPhone 18和iPhone 18e的生產技術合併，因此兩部機的差異可能會大幅縮細。

暫時未知這樣會令iPhone 18e變得更好，還是iPhone 18變差——但兩部機可能只會在螢幕面板和鏡頭上有少許分別。

總結

總括來說，假設iPhone Air最終沒有被砍（我當然希望不會）——之後的iPhone系列將會是新模式：秋季3部，春季再3部。最終這個做法有望讓Apple更好地劃分發布節奏，針對不同市場。

這樣也可能會推高iPhone的平均售價，因為想趁熱潮搶先購買的人會被迫選擇iPhone 18 Pro，而非平價型號。

分階段推出的策略最終能否讓每部機都賣得更好，還有待觀察，但這是初步的看法。

你怎麼看Apple將iPhone發布分階段的做法？你會在今年秋天購買，還是等到春天？不妨在留言區分享你的看法。
